:::{#def-data-splits}
#### Training/validation/test split

A **training/validation/test split** divides the observations $1, \ldots, \nobs$ of a data set
into three disjoint sets of indices,
$\trainidx$, $\validx$ and $\testidx$,
and takes the observations in $\trainidx$
as the [training set](#def-training-set):

$$
\ba
& \trainidx \cup \validx \cup \testidx = \set{1, \ldots, \nobs},
\\
& \trainidx \cap \validx = \emptyset,
\\
& \trainidx \cap \testidx = \emptyset,
\\
& \validx \cap \testidx = \emptyset,
\\
& \trainset = \paren{(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})}_{\iobs \in \trainidx}.
\ea
$$ {#eq-data-splits}

:::

:::{#rem-source-data-splits}
#### Source: Training/validation/test split

@james2021islr2e [pp. 198--201].

:::

::: {#exm-data-splits-sizes}
#### Split sizes for 32 cars

In @exr-data-splits,
a rule of 60% / 20% / 20% on $\nobs = 32$ cars
gives sets of 19, 6, and 7 cars,
and the 7 test cars are used only once, after the model is chosen.
:::
